requirement_results.evidence: masked_and.v matches ground truth structure exactly (and_same0/1, and_cross0/1, XOR combination, no registers); design_brief and fault_model describe the timing/glitch review focus without naming the vulnerability, consistent with hidden_spec mechanism.

Differential run shows golden_run exit_code 0 with all PASS, vulnerable_run (baseline) exit_code 1 with FR2/FR3/FR4/SR1/SR2/SR3 FAIL; baseline_run and mutation_baseline_run both confirm expected behavior.
requirement_results.requirement: Grader accepts correct submission and rejects baseline

requirement_results.evidence: FR1 covers schema_conformance, FR2/SR2 cover fault_coverage, FR3/SR1 cover leakage_detection_accuracy, FR4/SR3 cover hardening_precision -- all four declared metrics are exercised by concrete checks.
requirement_map lists FR1-FR4 as functional and SR1-SR3 as security, each with distinct detection logic and test files; per_requirement_coverage confirms all 7 covered with mutants detected 1/1 each.
requirement_results.requirement: Requirement map separates functional and security requirements

requirement_results.evidence: SR2 dynamically parses assign statements to extract true cross-term nets rather than hardcoding names; SR3 checks dataflow-graph-derived register placement rather than a generic keyword check; SR1 uses keyword+anti-phrase matching against vulnerability_summary content.
All Verilog/JSON/markdown files are plain text, no external dependencies beyond iverilog/vvp; sim_trace.vcd.txt is a human-readable stimulus table sufficient for cross-checking.

Task is specifically about glitch-induced first-order leakage in a masked AND gadget, a canonical side-channel/fault analysis scenario with concrete RTL, fault model, and hardening proposal requirements tied to real netlist structure.

evaluate.py has deterministic parsing, graceful fallback if iverilog unavailable, and every requirement id always emits PASS/FAIL with no silent skip or traceback risk (confirmed by FR1 malformed-JSON handling).

README.md, design_brief.md, fault_model.json, and metadata.json use neutral engineering language (timing/settling/review focus) without CWE ids, SR ids, or explicit vulnerability naming; masked_and.v has no security-flagging comments.
requirement_results.requirement: No leakage of hidden security intent in public artifacts

requirement_results.evidence: FR1-FR4 are each independently verifiable via schema/type checks, net-name matching against masked_and.v, algebraic invariant cross-check via iverilog/vvp, and dataflow traceability of registers_to_add -- not a single generic restatement.
requirement_results.requirement: Public functional requirements are concrete and machine-checkable
